Commentary.Commentary: That's all we have from a hard-fought series. New Zealand end their summer on a bright note with a series win. England, well, they are shaping well in the limited-overs cricket but aren't quite the same when it comes to the traditional format. They certainly need to pull their socks up. Right then, it's time to take your leave. Hope you have enjoyed our coverage. We look forward to your company in near future. Meanwhile, you can go to the concerned tab to catch all the updates from the Johannesburg Test. Until next time, it's goodbye and cheers!
Kane Williamson has been presented with the series trophy. He calls his teammates for some snapshots and they come with their heads held high. They pose and let out a huge roar. Played, New Zealand!

Victorious skipper, Kane Williamson starts by saying it has been a great win for them. Immediately credits England for being good competitors and then shifts the focus on his team. Adds a lot of steel was shown by the middle order, something they have been lacking for a while. On Boult and Southee, he says they are two of the best bowlers in the world and he's never worried about the new ball wickets with the pair around. Admits they didn't get off to the best start today and they knew it could turn out to be a tough day for them. Credits Latham, de Grandhomme and gives special mention to Wagner and Sodhi for sticking it out. Sums it up saying it turned out to be a great series and thanks the crowd for its support.

England skipper, Joe Root says they threw everything they had on New Zealand but admits the hosts batted really, really well. Says it's been a long tour for them and he is proud of his boys for doing well. Adds that barring the first innings in Auckland, it was a very close series. Reckons as a Test cricketer, you want to play a big series and they had the opportunity to do so. Accepts it hasn't gone as they would have liked but they'll take the good stuff from this week into the English summer.

Man of the Series, Trent Boult is really elated to get over the line in the end. Calls it a memorable win for them and credits his partner, Tim Southee for sharing the spoils with him. Adds they enjoy bowling together on such surfaces. Tells us that Test cricket is his favorite format and hopes to have a few more Test matches in the season.

Man of the Match, Tim Southee says it's been a rough couple of days for him (suffering from viral) but it's all good in the end. Adds that it's been a great summer for them and they are happy to end it on the right note. Tells us that there was something for the seamers in the pitch and it remained same throughout the five days. On Boult, he says he has played a lot of cricket with him and they enjoy a good partnership together. Ends saying it's a special series win for them and they will remember this for a long time.

Ish Sodhi, the man of the hour, is up for a chat with Simon Doull. He credits Wagner for the way he played out time with him in the middle. Continues praising him and states they discussed and kept themselves going by saying it's just a matter of 10-12 minutes. Is happy to get words of encouragement from his skipper near the boundary rope. Informs that he got one blow on the finger and that's pretty sore now but the job is done and that will help him forget it. Is disappointed with his performance with the ball but feels it's good to cover it up with the bat.

Two balls, two wickets - that's how Day 5 began. Stuart Broad was in his elements and the others also assisted him well. By Lunch, New Zealand were four down and staring down the barrel. Their last hope was pinned on the shoulders of Latham and Watling but the duo was dismissed in the afternoon session and a loss looked imminent. However, Colin de Grandhomme batted out of character to frustrate the English team, once he got out, the writing was on the wall with Tim Southee not fit to bat at his usual position. Then, New Zealand got two unlikely heroes in Ish Sodhi and Neil Wagner. The pair consumed 188 balls and snatched a draw from the jaws of defeat.

At one stage, England looked like running away with the show owing to their bowling performance on Day 2 but their bowling went flat on the following day and they ended with only a 29-run lead. The English batting fared exceedingly well in the second essay though and courtesy a strong batting show, they posted a target of 382 for the Kiwis. The New Zealand openers showed great resilience yesterday evening and this Test match entered Day 5 with England needing 10 wickets to level the series.

This was one heck of a Test match. England put to bat lost their way (5 for 94) and were revived through the century from Jonny Bairstow and his partnerships with the tail. Tim Southee and Trent Boult once again dominated proceedings to claim all ten wickets in the first innings. In reply, New Zealand were blown away by the might of Stuart Broad and company. Reduced to 5/36, they too got support from the lower order batsmen. BJ Watling and Colin de Grandhomme applied themselves to take it deep and then the Kiwi pace trio did an outstanding job with the bat to narrow the gap.

Phew, this one was for the purists! Those who like the big swing of the bat, powerful shots and bat dominating ball, they hopefully stayed away. Test cricket is alive and kicking. A blockathon to deny a win to the opposition. That too by the lower order batsmen. Cannot get better than this. New Zealand take the series 1-0, the good boys have won and they have avenged the loss in the shorter format.

Time is up! No new batsman coming in. The umpire tells that to the English skipper who has disappointment written all over his face. It's a draw. The players are shaking hands in the middle now. Ish Sodhi returns with his head held high. Gets a big warm hug from Kane Williamson. What an effort! Smiling faces all around in the Kiwi camp. The English players are distraught. They tried their heart out but cannot avoid going 13 consecutive away Tests without a win, their longest winless streak on the road. This is also the first time England have lost a Test series against New Zealand since 1999.

OUT! Wagner nearly survived by using the technology. A flatter ball landing outside off, probably a slider, Wagner stays back to defend but seems to have missed it. He gets rapped on the pads, they appeal and the umpire raises his finger after thinking for a while. Neil is quick to opt for the DRS. The replays roll in and the first frame detects an inside edge. Just when we thought he has survived, the third umpire takes further look at the replays and finds that Vince has caught the ball which had popped out at silly point. Not an lbw, but caught. Wagner's stubborn knock is over, he faced 103 balls and the last partnership consumed 188 balls. Wow, just wow.
Huge shout for an lbw! Up goes the finger and Neil Wagner takes the DRS immediately.
Lunges well forward and defends it with the inner half of the bat to square leg.
Quicker one, full and on off, Wagner brings his bat down in time and keeps it out.
Flighted and angled in on middle, Wagner defends it from the back foot.
Tossed up ball on middle, Sodhi defends it back. A maximum of 2 overs left now.
Too full and on middle, easily kept out on the leg side.
Fires in one, very full and on off, nothing can go through Sodhi today. He blocks again.
A full toss on off, Sodhi just taps it down safely.
Floated and full this time, Sodhi gets forward and defends it to silly point.
FOUR! Smashes another one away for a boundary. Fetches a short delivery from outside off and hammer-pulls it through mid-wicket.
We are done with the scheduled 98 overs for the day. There is still some time left, maybe three more overs and England are in a hurry to squeeze as much as they can.
Loopy and on off, defended off the front foot to end yet another over.
Flatter and on middle, Wagner lunges and defends it with the inner half of the bat.
Floated one on leg, Wagner works it off his pads towards leg gully.
Strides forward to a full ball and pushes it to silly point.
Wagner has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tossed up ball on off, turning in, Wagner defends it from the crease.
Still 7 minutes to go and we can squeeze in a couple of more overs. Jack Leach to continue...
Presses forward and defends a full ball calmly.
Sodhi has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter and on off, tapped down to point.
Gets forward to a full ball and blocks it safely.

FIFTY FOR SODHI! What a knock by him! He waited calmly for this moment. As soon as he spots a short ball around off, he goes back and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary. A knock to remember, a knock of character, a knock of resilience, a knock of utmost patience. Take a bow!
Starts with a flighted full ball on off, it's defended watchfully off the front foot.
New Zealand have almost braved it. Is there any more twist in the tale? Dawid Malan to bowl it...
Shout for a catch, not given! Spinning in from the rough outside off, Wagner looks to flick but it goes off the pads to short leg. England appeal but to no avail.
Hangs back to a flatter delivery and offers a stoic defense.
Gets to the pitch of the ball and kills it into the turf.
Flatter one on the stumps, another tight defense.
Neil has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated delivery outside off, Wagner takes a long stride forward to smother it away.
Root tries a bouncer but English skipper, let me tell you these two have been ducking since 22 overs. Easily countered.
Flatter one on the stumps, lunges ahead and defends.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Slower through the air outside off, Sodhi blocks well.
Very full in length, Ish defends into the ground.
Flatter ball on the stumps, blocked.
Joe Root into the attack. Umbrella field for Sodhi.... Barmy Army is still on top of its voice.
Quicker and flatter outside off, Wagner lets it be.
On middle and off, defended into the ground.
NW has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated delivery outside, another solid defense on offer. These two are doing it with ease.
Quicker and flatter in nature, Neil blocks it out.
Leach from around the wicket, pitched around middle and leg, Wagner presses ahead in defense.
Finishes the over with a bumper, no fuss for the Kiwi leggie. He ducks under it and walks to the other end with his head high. 4 more overs to survive!
Very full on the stumps, bunted back to Jimmy.
In the avenue of apprehension, Ish Sodhi shoulders his arms.
Fuller delivery and angling in on middle and off, Sodhi blocks.
Stays back to a length ball and defends it tightly.
On a length and closer to off stump, by now Sodhi knows where his stumps are. HE LEAVES! And leaves England in frustration...
Right then, England's go-to man James Anderson is called back. Can the veteran deliver? Come on Jimmy, screams the Barmy Army...
Tossed up ball on off, soundly defended to end yet another over.
Change of angle this time. Hurls in a tossed up ball from around the wicket, it's around leg and Wagner plays it off his pads towards short leg.
Keeps it full and on off, Wagner is content in keeping it out and he is doing so very intelligently.
Flighted on off, defended again off the front foot.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot.

Huge shout for an lbw! Not given. England don't have any review left. A flighted ball landing full on off, Wagner tries to defend but it spins back in and strikes him on the pads. They appeal their lungs out but the umpire shakes his head. The replays show that it would have missed leg.
Jack Leach with one final go now...
A touch short and on off, giving the chance to the batsman to go back and push it square of the wicket on the off side. Finds the gap and takes a run.
Looking for a magic delivery, the part-timer, bowls it very full and outside off, Wagner jams it out.
An extra slip comes in and there is a short mid-wicket now too.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Keeps it full and just outside off, Wagner tries to defend it with firm hands and gets it away safely to short leg.
Too full on this occasion, on off, Wagner is forward in defense.
Flighted and on off, Wagner with a long stride forward defends it on the leg side.
Possible 7 more overs to go, light permitting. Dawid Malan continues...
Edgy again but Sodhi has brought a truckload of luck! A pitched up delivery on off, Sodhi tries to drive but gets an inside edge. It rolls to one of the two short leg fielders.
Good length ball on middle, Sodhi closes the face of his bat and plays it calmly towards backward square leg.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Lands it on a length and outside off, shaping away, Sodhi makes an easy leave.

Oohhhh...that's so close to Root's right hand. A back of a length ball on middle, Sodhi tries to defend on the leg side but fails to control it. It comes from the shoulder of the bat and goes very closely past Root. He is there on his knees for those chances but was late in his reflexes.
Angling back into the batsman from a good length outside off, Sodhi defends it down.
Reaches out to that one and pushes it towards point.

Was that a googly? Oh yes, almost gets an edge! Wagner had no idea about it. He presses forward to defend but this one turns away with a bit of extra bounce off the rough. Beats the edge by a whisker.
Too full in length outside off, blocked towards silly point.
Quicker and fuller outside off, Wagner plants his front foot across as he makes a leave.
Stays behind the line and blocks, Wagner.
From around the wicket, pitched outside off, on a shorter length, defended off the back foot.

Slight halt in play. Physio is out again. Ish Sodhi has been in the firing line. He has taken quite a few blows on his body for his side. Takes one more on the last delivery and seems to be in pain. Once again, the umpires are keeping a close eye. All good now. Joe Root's final roll of the dice, maybe. DAWID MALAN, the leggie, the part-timer, is inserted into the attack. The rough outside the left-hander's off stump will assist him. Can he get his line and length right and become a hero here?

On the glove, again! Ish Sodhi has copped a blow again. He's hanging in out there for his side. Brave lad! Looks to go deep and keep this short ball out but gets it off the gloves as the ball dies down on the pitch. Again this could have gone into the hands, says Atherton with a mild voice.
Shortish outside off, punched off the back foot comfortably.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short and outside off, Sodhi with soft hands looks to defend it down but the ball takes the edge. Since he played that with delicate hands, the edge doesn't carry to the gully fielder.
Nicely played! Fuller delivery on off, Ish presses ahead to push it away.
Short but the line is wide outside off, easy leave for Sodhi.
Pitched up delivery on the stumps, Wagner negotiates another over.
This bumper is high enough for Neil to have time to duck under.

Flush on the elbow! Didn't know much about it, says Mike Atherton on air. So true! Broad with a well-directed short ball, it keeps getting bigger. Wagner is a touch late in ducking and cops a blow on the right elbow. OUCH!
Short on leg, Neil Wagner ducks at last.
Fuller on off, blocked towards silly point.

FOUR! Runs for New Zealand! Broad bowls a similar delivery which he bowled to start Day 5 - A half-volley on leg stump, Wagner moves across and clips it past the two men - short fine leg and leg gully for a boundary.
Another one sprayed down leg, Ish once again fails to put that away.
Strays down leg does Stokes, Sodhi misses his flick shot.
Shortish from Ben, Sodhi calmly ducks under it.
Ish defends it from within the crease.
Hug appeal, no says the umpire! Angling in from a length around off and pings Sodhi on the pads. Stokes appeals but the height seems to be an issue there.
Now comes Stokes into the attack. He goes wide of the crease and angles a length delivery down leg, Sodhi looks to pull it away but it goes off the thigh pad to the left of the keeper.
Fuller in length on the leg stump, defended down on the leg side.
Fuller and on the pads, worked towards square leg.
Shorter delivery on middle and off, ducked under.

Up in the air... Ish Sodhi survives again! Caaaaatcccccchhh it, screams Broad in anger. Dear me! The lady luck just refuses to be with England. Snorter from Broad, kicks off from the surface as Sodhi fends it away from the body. The ball takes the handle and lobs over gully. James Vince there backtracks and then leaps to take it with his right hand. Sigh, can't get to it as the ball falls safely. They take a single.
Strange way to stand at silly point. Joe Root is on his knees, not even standing. England are also on their knees at the moment with lady luck evading them.
Goes back deep in the crease and tucks it towards short leg.
Continues to bombard short stuff, Sodhi is happy to duck and let it sail over him.
Flatter and fuller on off, blocked safely to the off side. Another over negotiated safely.
Too full this time, Neil defends it by prodding forward.
Once again turning back in sharply from outside off, Wagner offers no shot and takes it on his pads.
Sharp spin and bounce into the batsman, from the rough, Wagner fails to defend and is hit high on the front pad.
Flighted and landing outside off, turning back in, Wagner defends it from the back foot.
Too full on off, defended to silly point.
Jack Leach is back from the other end.
Back of a length on middle, shown straight bat.

FOUR! More luck for Sodhi! Broad after banging short, goes fuller and angles it wider outside off. Sodhi reaches out to that one. Gets a fat edge which flies over the slip cordon for a streaky boundary.
Banged short again, Sodhi drops his wrists to make another leave.
Shortish on leg, fended away on the leg side.
Digs in another short one, angling away towards off, Sodhi arches back and evades it.
Shortish delivery from Broad from around the wicket angle, Sodhi has got nothing to do with it. He ducks.
Stuart Broad returns. One final attempt it seems from him. Plenty of close-in fielders waiting desperately for one error. Test cricket at its best.

Drinks break. 14 overs left. The Kiwi lower order is providing good resistance. England are trying hard but seems the luck is not on their side as a few chances didn't carry. Into the final hour we head, let's see what happens...
Wood fires a fuller ball on off, Wagner defends it solidly.
Stays behind the line and offers a straight bat.
Short ball, from over the wicket, Wagner fends it wide of the man at short leg.
Wagner rises on his toes to tap this short ball down.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.

Another one that evades the fielder! Wood is bowling his heart out but is just not able to pick up a wicket. Hits the deck hard again, angles it away on off, Sodhi tries to fend it away but this time the ball goes off the shoulder of the bat. There are two gullies in place but the ball evades them. A single taken. Frustration continues for England.
This one doesn't turn! On the rough again, Neil Wagner plays for the turn but this one goes on with the arm. Beats the outside edge of Wagner's bat.
Flighted delivery, pitching on the rough and turning in a touch, Wagner covers it with a lunge and blocks.
A bit too full outside off, jammed out off the front foot.
Turning in from a length outside off, Wagner goes back in defense.
Pitches it on the rough, Wagner takes a stride forward and keeps it out.
Tossed up delivery outside off, Wagner prods forward and defends.
Pushes this fuller delivery through cover and calls for a single.
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, Wagner hangs back in defense.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.

In the air... off the gloves and evades the gully fielder! Hands on head for the English players. These Kiwis are riding some serious luck! Wood with all his might bangs in a short delivery and gets it to bounce a touch extra to catch Sodhi off guard. The Kiwi leggie is put into a tangle as he awkwardly tries to sway away from the line with his bat dangling out. The ball takes the gloves and lobs wide of the diving gully fielder. And they take a single. Hostile stuff from Wood.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Digs in a short delivery around leg, Sodhi hops and fends it away.
Change of ends for Mark Wood. Let's see if this works.
Takes a long stride forward and blocks it solidly.
Floated delivery outside off, Wagner presses ahead and defends.
Flatter and quicker ball outside off, Wagner lets it pass.
Turn and bounce for Root! Turning away from a length outside off, NW stays back to defend but gets an edge wide of the slip fielder.
Wagner prods forward and meets this tossed up delivery with a straight bat.
Fuller and fired outside off, Wagner pushed it towards cover.
Joe Root brings himself back on.
Lunges ahead to a tossed up ball and buries it into the turf.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up delivery down the leg side, Sodhi doesn't offer any shot. Bairstow behind the stumps fails to collect it cleanly.
Quicker one around middle and leg, worked towards short leg off the back foot.
Flatter through the air outside off, Sodhi with a little stride forward smothers it away.
Flighted delivery outside off, blocked in front of the silly point fielder.
Watches the short ball till the last moment and crouches low to let it sail over him to the keeper. This is good stuff from Wagner.
Shortish and around middle and off, Wagner places it through point. They don't run though.
Once again Wood hits the deck hard, aims at the body of the batsman, Wagner sits under it again.
Bangs short again, Wagner rises on his toes and safely taps it on the pitch.
Fuller in length and angling away towards off, Neil looks to defend but gets it off the outer edge towards the point fielder.

Short delivery on middle and leg, Wagner is quick to take evasive action as he ducks under it. After the end of the last over, a substitute fielder came out with the drinks, wonder why as no one was looking for it. Returned immediately.
Flattish in nature, IS blocks it out watchfully this time.
Flighted ball around leg, turning away, Sodhi gets down on one knee to bring out the big slog. Misses it completely.
Leach comes from around the wicket and pitches it outside leg, Sodhi pads it away.
Slower through the air around middle and off, blocked into the ground.
Flatter delivery around middle and leg, Ish Sodhi jams it out towards short leg.
Flighted delivery outside off, defended in front of the silly point fielder.
Short and down leg, easy duck for Wagner.
Short and angling away towards off, Neil pushes it away from the body. The ball hits the sticker of his bat and bounces in front of Cook at silly point.
Wagner takes his bottom hand off on this short ball as he defends it down.

Just past the diving square leg fielder! Shortish delivery, climbing on Sodhi who hops across and fends it away. It goes uppishly towards square leg but just wide of the diving Vince at square leg. A single taken. Lucky, Ishhhh!
Is right back to a short ball and drops it back down on the pitch.
Shortish delivery from around the wicket, Sodhi hops back and taps it beside the pitch.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot to end the over.

Oh dear, the short leg fielder takes a beating. Sodhi unfurls another firm pull shot and it hits Cook on the back. The ball deflects to mid-wicket and they take a run. Few concerned faces surround the former English skipper but he gives a thumbs up. You don't often see senior players fielding in a close-in position at bat-pad. One of my colleagues, with the memory of an elephant, pings - In a Mumbai Test match involving India and Australia in 2001, Sachin Tendulkar pulled one of those rubbish short balls and it hit Justin Langer on the back at short leg and then ballooned in the air. A certain Ricky Ponting who was stationed at short mid-wicket caught a stunner then off the deflection. Hmmm...speaking of Punter, he was also one of those senior players who used to field at silly point or short leg, that too without a helmet, which we don't recommend.
FOUR! Just a fractionally short of a length ball and Sodhi once again has a crack at it. Connects well and smashes it in front of square leg for a boundary.
Loopy and on off, defended off the front foot.
Spinning in from around off, defended off the back foot.
FOUR! A gentle loosener, short and around off, Ish goes deep inside the crease and powers his pull shot over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Physio comes out. Maybe to have a look at Wagner. But the umpire sends him back quickly. Meanwhile, Joe Root returns in the attack.
Rising delivery again, around off, Wagner remains back and somehow keeps it out safely on the off side.
Short around rib cage, Wagner fends at it awkwardly. He gets hit on the elbow.
Back over the wicket and Wood bangs it short around leg, Wagner ducks.
Goes on his toes and defends a shortish ball to covers.
Back of a length delivery outside off, straightening a bit, Wagner pushes inside the line and misses.
Bouncer to Wagner, around off, he leaves it alone.
Flatter and turning in sharply, Wagner pushes it defensively past silly point for a run.
Floated and on off, spinning in, Wagner is on the front foot as he defends it towards silly point.
Leans forward and pushes it through covers for one.
Loopy and outside off, left alone.
Tossed up ball on off, defended to silly point.
Flighted ball on off, turning away, Sodhi leaves it.
Stays back, hops a bit and fends it towards silly point.
Short again from Wood, he's bending his back, Neil is happy to sit under it.
Too much venom! Short delivery, angling in on the body, Wagner ducks but the ball goes behind off his shoulders. They appeal but not given.
Neil defends it from within the crease.
Slightly shorter in length on middle, defended with a straight bat.
Wood bangs in a short one on middle, it keeps climbing as Wagner ducks at the very last moment.
Sodhi presses ahead and defends well.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Shot! Ish Latham? Flighted delivery on the stumps, Sodhi gets down and nails the sweep in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Goes back to defend but gets an inside edge on the pads.
What a delivery! Pitching around leg and turning away towards off. Sodhi presses forward to defend but the ball turns away to beat the outside edge of his bat. Closeeee!
From over the wicket, Leach pitches it around leg, Sodhi pads it away.
Shortish delivery on middle and off, Wagner pushes it towards point.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Good length ball outside off, defended off the back foot.
Fuller delivery on the stumps, blocked out.
Neil Wagner is in next. He wagged nicely in the first innings. Can he emulate?

OUT! Colin de Grandhomme, what have you done? Like what? What were you thinking? Credit to England again for being patient and sticking to their plan. They got Watling earlier and now they have netted the big fish. Wood from around the wicket bangs one short on leg and wants the batsman to take on the challenge. De Grandhomme says enough is enough and accepts it which ultimately proves to be his undoing. He pulls one and it goes towards fine leg where Jack Leach comes a couple of steps ahead and grabs a good low catch. Colin smashes his bat into his pads in frustration as he walks back to the dressing room. Good change from Root and once again it brings him a wicket. Three more needed for England.

Wood comes from around the wicket and bowls a short ball outside leg, de Grandhomme, at first was interested in going after it but in the end chooses the safest option. Moves inside the line and leaves it.
Mark Wood is back on.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter ball around middle and off, Sodhi stands back in defense.
Flighted delivery, landing outside off, Sodhi blocks.
Takes a long stride forward and blocks it out gently.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up on off, pushed towards cover.

FOUR! Top edge and it goes fine again! More frustration for England! Broad digs in another short ball, Colin once again takes on the challenge of pulling it. This time he gets it off the top edge which goes fine down the leg side.

FOUR! Nicely done! Brings up the 50-run stand between the two! What a show they have put on. Shortish again on middle and leg, helped away with a pull by de Grandhomme. It bisects the man at deep square leg and fine leg and races away to the fence.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Shortish and again on leg stump, helped down to fine leg for a single.

Daylight between bat and ball, screams our scorer Aakash as he sees the Hot Spot. England lose a review. Shortish delivery down leg, Sodhi runs out of patience as he tries to help it away. Seems to have missed it completely as Bairstow behind the stumps collects it by moving swiftly to his left. They all go up in an appeal but umpire Erasmus stays put. Root, more in desperation takes the DRS. No bat seen on the replays.
An appeal for a caught down the leg side is turned down by the umpire. Root takes the review which looks more in desperation.
Short one on middle, Sodhi bends his back and lets it sail.
Flighted delivery on off, defended into the leg side this time.
Some more loop, landed full on off, killed into the turf.
CdG has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Takes a stride ahead and smothers it away.
Floated delivery outside off, blocked solidly off the front foot.
Fuller outside off to begin this new spell, it's pushed towards cover.

Jack Leach is brought back into the attack. Micheal Atherton informs us something. England have kept their 12th man on the boundary rope so that no time is wasted in retrieving the ball. So tight is the game.
Now ducks under a short ball in time. Good passage of play for the Kiwis.

FOUR! 48-run stand between the two now. They are going well at the moment and England are starting to feel pressure now. Full and too straight from Broad, Sodhi shuffles across and clips it deftly down to fine leg for a boundary.
On a length and straightening a touch, Sodhi is a bit squared up but still he manages to keep it out.
Good solid defense from Sodhi as he leans forward, his head falls towards the line of the ball and he keeps it out.
Once again goes low, covers the stumps and pushes it back to Broad.
Fuller in length and angling in on middle, Ish Sodhi crouches low in his stance as he jams it out.
Good length ball on middle, de Grandhomme looks to push it back but his bottom hand comes off and he mistimes it back to Jimmy.
Drops it somewhere near short and good length mark, Colin is right behind the line as he stabs it out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Very full at the base of middle, knocked to mid on firmly.
Anderson tries to keep it full but ends up delivering it a bit too straight, de Grandhomme flicks it easily off the pads down to long leg and collects a brace.
Doesn't fiddle with a length ball which is outside off.
Gets across to a length delivery on middle, IS tucks it on the leg side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fullish outside off, defended with a stride forward.
Veering on the pads, helped fine down the leg side for a single.
FOUR! Finally gets a boundary, CdG! Broad tries to bowl a short ball but this came at a good height for the batter. Colin stays back and pulls it firmly through mid-wicket.
Bangs one short on middle, CdG ducks under it.
Is a tad late in bringing his bat down to a fuller ball and hence gets it off the inside edge behind square on the leg side for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Just over the off stump! Anderson hurls one around off, it keeps coming back in, Colin de Grandhomme lets it come and then shoulders his arms. Wasn't a good leave I would say but he trusted the bounce.
Length ball in the direction outside off, left alone without much fuss.
Fuller and curling back in on middle, worked off the inner half towards square leg.
Length delivery, closer to the off stump line, Colin makes a good leave.
Fuller delivery and attacking the stumps, Ish crouches low, gets across and bunts it towards mid on.
Pounds a short one on middle and leg, Sodhi ducks.
Drops it on a shorter length outside off, the Kiwi leggie stays right behind the line to keep it out.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Ish Sodhi stabs it out towards point.

Short ball on middle and leg, Colin de Grandhomme swivels a touch and helps the pull through backward square leg for a single. He's willing to give strike to Sodhi, showing good confidence in his partner.
Covers the line and nicely defends it off the back foot.
Gets forward to a full delivery and pats it to mid off.
Short of a length delivery outside off, pushed away towards point.
Marginally fuller on off, blocked out well.

Sodhi copped a blow in the previous over and seems it is hurting him. He calls for the physio and asks for some assistance. The grim look on his face tells us how badly that must have stung him. A bit of a delay...

Huge appeal for a catch down leg, turned down! Anderson strays around the pads, Sodhi shuffles across to flick it away but it goes off something behind. Bairstow flies to his left and takes it. Appeals for it but umpire Oxenford isn't interested. Good call, it went off his thigh pad.
Gets across and clips it behind square on the leg side for a single.
De Grandhomme is on the back foot to this length delivery as he pushes it away towards point. These two now have eaten up 100 balls, good going!
Outside off, Sodhi is all smiles as he makes an easy leave.
Ouch! Broad hits the deck hard, Sodhi is ready to take evasive action as he ducks under it but this one doesn't bounce much as he expected it to be. Cops a blow on the left elbow.
Broads hurls it on a length outside off, Sodhi stays back to defend but ekes out a thick inside edge on the back pad.
In the corridor outside off, Ish Sodhi shoulders his arms to it.
Bangs in a short one on middle, Sodhi sits under it.
FOUR! Too straight from Broad and Sodhi picks up a boundary! Good length delivery, angling in on middle and leg, Ish moves inside the line and deflects it off his pads down to fine leg.
Stuart Broad to have a go from the other end.
In that tempting channel outside off, de Grandhomme is happy to shoulder his arms.
Fuller in length and angling in, Colin brings his bat down in time as he bunts it out.
Back of a length delivery, angling in on middle, Sodhi walks across the sticks and clips it down to fine leg to get off strike.
Slightly shorter in length, once again outside off, Ish shows a tight defense.
Almost... On a length and skidding a bit off the deck, Sodhi looks to have a tentative poke at it and nearly, nearly edges one behind.
Anderson begins with a good length delivery on off, Sodhi stays back and pushes at it away from the body.

Welcome back for the final time in this Test. Kudos! We have got to witnesses all the 15 sessions, which is seldom seen these days. Well, England have one more black-coloured opponent in front of them apart from the Black Caps. Any guesses? Yes, the Dark Clouds! The light is bound to fade every minute from now on, however, for the moment there is sunlight. The visitors have the new ball and would be hoping for it to do its magic. De Grandhomme and Ish Sodhi are out in the middle. The latter will face James Anderson.
... Day 5, Final Session ...

A couple of wickets in the session and England have inched closer to levelling the series. However, they have a big battle in hand, against natural forces, as the light is fading considerably. As far as the action of the afternoon session is considered, New Zealand lost both Latham and Watling which very much pushed them on the back foot. Currently, Colin de Grandhomme and Ish Sodhi are fighting but have not looked convincing. 39 overs to go in the day, however, it looks unlikely we will get all, given the way it has turned gloomy. Do join us in a short while.
The English players quickly change their positions in the field, wanting to have one extra over. But it doesn't matter. The umpires look at the clock and decide, it's time for Tea.
Another full ball, this time outside off, Colin covers the line and allows it through.
FOUR! Fuller this time, around off, it's driven firmly down the ground through mid off for a boundary.
A length delivery outside off, holding its line, de Grandhomme shoulders arms.
Too full and speared into the batsman, Sodhi tries to flick but gets a leading edge towards point. A single.
Full and on middle, defended to mid-wicket.
Wood continues and is given the second new ball. He bowls it around off, angling in, Sodhi flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
On the driving length outside off, holding its line, Colin allows it through to the keeper.
Around off on a length, de Grandhomme defends it from the crease to the leg side.
Angling into the batsman from around off, on a length, Sodhi flicks it off his pads through backward square leg for a single.
Straighter in line, solidly defended from the crease by Sodhi.
Full again, around off, de Grandhomme plays it out to covers for a single.
Full and around off, some visible inswing, de Grandhomme defends it.

Out come the jackets for the umpires. Seems it's too cold out there. Meanwhile, the second new ball has been taken. It's James Anderson back into the attack. Four slips in pace. 10 minutes to tea, exciting phase, this.
Switches to over the wicket and bangs in a bouncer again, Ish sits underneath it.
Two short legs in place now along with the leg gully. The length becomes predictable then. It's short around leg, Sodhi ducks.
Good length ball around middle and leg, helped off the pads to the leg side.
Attempts a yorker but ends up serving a low full toss around off, Sodhi digs it out back to the bowler.
Runs out of patience this time. Hard for the tailenders to focus so much. Identical to the last delivery, this time Sodhi tries to glance but misses.
Wood continues from around the wicket with a leg gully in place. Bowls a short delivery on leg, Sodhi allows it through.
Loopy around off, Colin is forward in defense. They are rushing through their overs.
Too full and off, once again blocked off the front foot.
Flighted full on off, de Grandhomme defends it off his front foot.
Around off, Colin defends it from the crease.
Goes on the back foot again and blocks.
Flatter and outside off, defended from the crease off the outer half of the bat to point.
Change of ends for Jack Leach.
Wood charges in from around the wicket and delivers a shortish ball around middle and leg, Sodhi shuffles and tries to flick but misses.
Goes full with his length outside off and de Grandhomme drives it through covers for three runs.
Another short ball and Sodhi fends at it with great discomfort. Fends it a bit uppishly but wide of short leg for a run.
Shortish and on off, defended down in front of short leg.
Bangs in a bouncer on middle, Sodhi ducks.
Short and on off, pulled to deep square leg for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
During the change of overs, the umpires called for light enhancing glasses.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Walks down the track and works it through mid-wicket for one.
Walks down to the pitch of the delivery and defends it.
Colin  has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy off spinner landing outside off, de Grandhomme gets forward to defend it near his front pad. Not sure whether he got bat onto it.
Smart thinking by Wood. Slips in a yorker around off, Sodhi however does well to dig it out.
Bowls it short and de Grandhomme pulls it behind square leg. Stokes sprints across to his right in the deep to stop the ball. A single taken.
Clouds are building up. England will not want any interruption due to bad light or rain.
Short and around leg, de Grandhomme fends it down awkwardly towards short leg.
Angles in a length ball on off, de Grandhomme defends it back from the crease.
Walks across the stumps and works it behind square leg for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, Sodhi allows it through.
Mark Wood is back into the attack.
Nicely tossed up and wide outside off, de Grandhomme pads it away.
Loopy off spinner on off, spinning in and beating Colin in his forward defensive prod. He is hit on the pads, once again a stifled appeal but nothing doing.
Very full and on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Turning back into the batsman from outside off, de Grandhomme goes back to defend but misses. A slight appeal from Root.
Walks forward and across to a full ball and pushes it with the spin on the leg side.
An off spinner landing full outside off, Colin tries to defend but misses and is hit on the pads.
Tries to defend it off his front foot but it skids back in to grab the inside edge. It rolls to square leg.
Tossed up and outside off, Sodhi blocks it off his front leg.
Defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flighted on off, Sodhi plays the paddle sweep down to long leg and takes a couple.
Shortish and outside off, cut straight to point.
Beauty of a delivery. Drifting into the batsman and landing full around off, Sodhi tries to play the line but it spins away to beat the outside edge.
Flatter full on off, turning in, Sodhi leans to defend it but it takes the inner edge and goes past short leg for a run.
Allows the ball to spin back in and keeps it out to mid-wicket.
Too full and outside off, Sodhi hits it hard but fails to beat the extra cover fielder.
Presses forward and pushes it with the spin to the leg side.
Gets forward and across to defend it with the spin to short leg.
Flighted full ball on off, defended off the front foot.
Once again takes his front leg to the pitch of the ball and shoos it away.
Plants his front foot across and pads it away.
Slower through the air, drags his length back a touch, de Grandhomme smothers it away.
Loops it up outside off, Colin presses forward in defense.
Very full, almost a yorker on the stumps, kept out.
Quicker and flatter through the air outside off, Colin de Grandhomme stays back to defend but gets it off the edge past second slip for a couple.
Sodhi has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! That's a good shot. There are a couple of short leg fielders and Sodhi has swept that fine to beat both. It races through backward square leg for a boundary. Brilliant.

Big appeal, first for the lbw and then for the bat-pad. Nothing from the umpire. It's spinning in and the batsman fails to defend. Gets hit on the pads and Root appeals. Then it lobs up to short leg who catches it. Now they all appeal. The umpire is having none of it.
Flighted and wide outside off, Sodhi hits it firmly to covers.
Bowls it full and around off, Sodhi defends it.
Presses forward and defends a full delivery watchfully.
Tries to cover the spin and block but it takes the inside edge and goes to fine leg for a run.
Sodhi has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Too full and outside off, Sodhi keeps it out from the outer half of the bat.
Skidding into the pads, it's clipped through mid-wicket for a brace.

Call it dropped if you want but that went in and out in the blink of an eye. Sodhi tried flicking against the turn and closed the face of the bat early. It popped out from the leading edge and the silly point fielder failed to hold on to the catch.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Nice drift and spin on this occasion as Colin tries to defend it off his front foot. Fails to put bat on ball but the impact is outside off.
Spinning in, flicked past short leg.
Another watchful defensive shot by de Grandhomme. Forced to play his unnatural game here.
Full and on off, defended watchfully.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Around off, de Grandhomme defends it off his back foot.
Too full and outside off, driven off the front foot to covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Fuller and on off, defended off the front foot.
Ish Sodhi is in next.

OUT! Is that Vince? No, it can't be. Oh yes, it is James Vince. Hard to believe he has taken a catch, that too a brilliant one. Trying to convince us that he is a good fielder. Umm...maybe he is but in the outfield, not in the slip cordon for sure. Has dropped twice while manning that region. Leach comes up with a loopy full ball landing around off, it turns back in with some extra bounce as we see some puff of dust also coming off the surface. Latham, who usually is a great sweeper of the ball, attempts it but fails to middle it properly. It flies behind square leg, James Vince is in the deep and he charges forward. Dives to complete the catch inches above the surface. Great effort. Just keep him in the outfield, England. Meanwhile, this brings a fighting knock by Tom Latham to an end. Probably, the final nail in the coffin. Runs are irrelevant so he shouldn't have played the shot, feels Simon Doull on air. Michael Atherton with a good counter, he says you just cannot sit back and block everything. Fair points by both. The margin is very thin.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Tossed up ball outside off, left alone.
Jack Leach replaces Wood in the attack, chance of ends for him. Always a good move to give your spinner chance to bowl from both ends.
Presses forward to a full ball and defends it to end the over.
Once again de Grandhomme is rapped on the pads as he fails to defend an off spinning delivery. They appeal but the impact remains an issue.
Spinning back in from outside off, Colin tries to defend but misses and is hit on the pads.
FOUR! Shot! This one is a touch too full outside off, de Grandhomme latches onto the width on offer and drills it through covers for a cracking boundary.
De Grandhomme has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Spinning in first up, not picked by Colin. Tries to drive but misses. It skids in to catch his thigh pad before scooting behind for a couple of leg byes.
Joe Root comes into the attack.

Drinks break. A good hour for England, although they picked only one wicket, it was a big one in the form of BJ Watling. Since the fall of that wicket, they've been all charged up. Colin de Grandhomme is living dangerously and one can smell that a wicket is just round the corner. Got to give it to Tom Latham who is fighting a lone battle and has largely looked untroubled.
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, Tom Latham hangs back and tucks it away towards mid-wicket. A maiden!
On a length and outside off, Tom hops back to keep it out.
Goes short again does Wood, but this time the line is down leg, easily ducked under.
Wood once again bangs in a short one on middle and leg, Tom ducks under it.
Short of a length delivery outside off, defended off the back foot.
Back of a length delivery around off, Latham defends it from the back foot to the leg side.
De Grandhomme has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter and full outside off, driven firmly but straight to the cover fielder.

Bowling with a gully now, Leach. He tosses it up and lands it outside off, skidding in, de Grandhomme offers no shot and takes it on the pads. They appeal but it's not doing enough to hit the timber, feels the umpire.
Tosses it up and outside off, spinning away, this time Colin allows it through.
Again an uppish drive. A flighted full ball on off, spinning away, de Grandhomme slices his cover drive but it goes safely to point.
Edged but safe! Colin drives a full ball against the spin, gets a thick outside edge but there is no second slip or gully there. A couple taken.
A bit short and outside off, played down to point.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
Back of a length delivery on middle and leg, defended on the on side.
A length ball outside off, Tom drives it off the front foot to mid off.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Digs in a short delivery, Latham leaves.
Defends it rather solidly and ends the over safely.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Gets on the front foot and drives it back to the bowler.

Oohh...just short of the cover fielder. This is why the spinner is brought in. Colin will attack him come what may. Flighted full delivery outside off, de Grandhomme drives it through the line, it's uppish as he goes hard at it and the cover fielder attempts for the catch with a dive to his left. But it falls just short and sneaks past him. They collect a couple. Nervy moment for the Kiwi all-rounder.
Goes back to an arm ball and punches it towards mid-wicket.
Time for some spin! Leach tosses it up around off and de Grandhomme drives it to covers.
Outside off, Latham makes a leave to end the over.
Lets the ball go outside his off stump.

David Lloyd with the eye of an eagle. He spots that unlike Stuart Broad, Mark Wood doesn't keep the ball in his right hand while running in his delivery stride. He keeps it in his left hand and just before delivering, he shifts it in his right. Also jokes that most bowlers like to feel the seam of the ball, know where the shine of the ball is etc which is impossible in this case with Mark Wood.
Short and angling down the leg side, Latham tries to glance but misses.
A little short in length and on middle, Latham glances it through square leg for a couple.
Shortish on off, defended off the back foot by Latham.
Short in length around leg, Colin pulls it powerfully to deep square leg for a run.
Anderson angles in a length ball on middle, Latham defends it on the leg side.
Latham has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Half-volley and put away in style. It's outside off and Latham drives it handsomely through covers for a glorious boundary. Moves to 81!
Another back foot defense by Tom.
Good length ball angling into the batsman, Latham defends it from the back foot.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Wood bends his back to go short again, around leg, Colin sways away from the line.
Digs in a short ball on middle and leg, Latham plays it down to mid-wicket and takes a single.
Shortish around leg, nicely nudged down to fine leg for a run.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.

Nearly another wicket! Wood delivers a sharp ball, a well-directed short ball, Latham tries to pull but gloves it over the keeper. They take a couple. Wood cannot believe his luck. He has a fielder at leg gully waiting for any error but this went over Bairstow.
Bouncer around off, Latham leaves it easily.
Goes inside the crease and tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman drives this through the covers. They pick up a single.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Full and around off, driven to mid off.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

FOUR! Colin de Grandhomme will not shy away from playing the pull shot. This is how he batted in the first innings as well. Attack is the best form of defence. Receives a short ball and pummels it to fine leg for a boundary.
Shortish and around leg, defended down to short leg.
Colin de Grandhomme is in next.

OUT! Can you believe it? There was a trap set for BJ Watling and he has fallen straight into it. The English team is jubilant, they have reduced New Zealand into half now. Five more needed. This is what happened - Wood has a leg gully in place and changes his angle from around the wicket. Watling expected some short pitch bowling and as a result premeditates his movement on the back leg. Shuffles across the sticks but to his surprise, it's a length ball in the line of the stumps. Watling plays the flick shot off his pads but straight into the hands of James Anderson at leg slip. He makes no mistake and this is a big breakthrough for England.
Good length ball around middle and off, defended.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.

Mark Wood is back into the attack. Stuart Broad is removed, a bit strange. Maybe, Joe Root wants his prime bowlers to be properly rested and rotated. At some point of time, if needed, the second new cherry will be available and he will need his best bowlers then. Joe is a proactive captain, foreseeing things.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, once again going across the batsman with the angle, Latham doesn't fiddle with it.
Full and around off, it's pushed off the front foot to covers.
Misses out, there. An overpitched delivery outside off, Latham plays a well-timed cover drive but finds the fielder.
Anderson takes this length delivery away from the left-hander, goes on with the angle and Latham covers his stumps before shouldering his arms.
Wicket to wicket line, serving it on a length, Latham is comfortably behind the delivery as he defends it to the off side.
Fractionally short and around off, Latham defends it off his back foot to short cover.
Once again Watling defends it well to end the over. So far so good from the Kiwis.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
A silly mid off in place now.
FOUR! Lovely shot, that's a beautiful drive. Broad serves it on a length and outside off, Watling nicely gets behind the line and creams it through mid off for a boundary.
In the channel outside off, Watling allows it through to the keeper.
Good length ball around off, Watling gets a bit opened up as he defends it to the off side.

Full and angling down the leg side, from around the wicket, Latham flicks it through backward square leg and Stoneman gives it the chase. Does well to slide near the rope and pull it back. Saves a run for his side.
HAMMER is out! No, it's not TRIPLE H. And it's not WRESTLEMANIA yet. It's one of the groundsmen trying to level up the bowler's landing area.
Blocks it from the crease to end the over. Looking solid and not providing any opening.
Back of a length ball on off, Watling keeps it out a bit awkwardly to the leg side.
Another back foot defense offered by Watling.
Angling in from around off, BJ blocks it watchfully from the crease.
On a length again, around off, Watling defends it from the crease.
Fine shot! Anderson serves it on a good length outside off, Latham stays back, lets the ball come under his eyes and then punches it past the left side of the point fielder for three runs.
Good line. Around off and angling in, Watling is solidly behind the line in defense.
Good length ball on middle and leg, Watling tries to help it on the leg side but fails to middle it properly. It drops on the pitch.
Width on offer outside off, on the shorter side, Watling cuts it from the back foot but finds the point fielder.
Broad bowls an inswinger here, around middle and off, Watling works it off his pads to square leg.
Hurls a length delivery wide outside off, Watling watches the line closely and then lets it through to the keeper. He is a good leaver of the ball, a key skill in his batting.
Off line first up. But it's the similar one which got him the wicket of Jeet Raval this morning. Latham though is more in control of his flick shot and eases it behind square leg for a single.
No surprise there. Stuart Broad is unleashed from the other end. Two slips and a gully for him as well.
Keeps his line around off and brings this one in, Watling closes the face of the bat and helps it to square leg. A maiden to begin with.
Lands it on a length around off, shaping away a bit, Watling rocks back and plays it down towards the cover-point fielder.
Jimmy pitches it up and around off, BJ drives it off his front foot to mid off. A good confident footwork shown by the Kiwi keeper.
Sharp movement this time. It nips back in from around off, Watling fails to keep it out and gets hit on the pads. No appeal as it's going down leg.
Good length ball again, around off, once more Watling defends it off his back foot towards the cover region.
Starts with a good length ball on off, Watling defends it from the crease to the leg side.
Senior bowler, James Anderson to kickoff proceedings. Watling on strike. Two slips and a gully in place.

We're back with the coverage and so are the players on the field. England enjoyed the morning session and would like to make merry in the afternoon also. The current Kiwi pair, however, stand in their way at the moment. Both Latham and Watling have looked solid and would try their best to keep the touring team at bay. Let's see who succeeds...
... DAY 5, SESSION 3 ...

There is some turn on offer for the spinners (although nothing like we see on Day 5 in the sub-continent) and reverse for the seamers. Tom Latham has shown great positivity and has stroked a half century. Will he stay there and continue to get support? Or will England come out all guns blazing just as they did this morning and clean them up? Join us in a short while to find out...

Amidst Broad's heroics, it was debutant Jack Leach who found a place for himself in the wicket's tally. He removed Ross Taylor and then James Anderson came roaring back to pick one to his name. All of a sudden the hosts lost four wickets and the hopes of them batting it out almost went out of the window. But... Tom Latham, who's batting since yesterday didn't let the hara-kiri disturb his concentration and batted with a lot of determination. BJ Watling, who was good in his first essay, lent him the desired support as together they have stitched a stand that is worth 33 (85) but it's even more worth as it has stopped England from creating further inroads.

We reckoned it to be an action-packed morning session and it didn't let us down. All thanks to Stuart Broad who just didn't let us shut our eyes. He steamed in with the Barmy Army right behind him and nipped out two wickets - Jeet Raval and Kane Williamson in successive deliveries to rock the Kiwis early. He bowled with a lot of venom and threatened to run away with the show.
Fuller delivery right on the off stump, Tom Latham presses forward in defense. LUNCH ON DAY 5!
Very full and fired into the stumps, Tom keeps it out on the leg side.
Stays put in the crease and dabs it square on the off side to pick up a couple of runs.
Angles it in on middle and off, Tom stays back to defend but gets an inside edge on the pads.
Slightly fuller outside of, blocked solidly by the southpaw.
Outside off, Tom Latham has got nothing to do with it.
Last over before Lunch...
Length delivery outside off, dealt off the back foot gently.
Drops it on a back of a length on middle, Watling punches it towards cover.
On a fuller length outside off, driven on the up towards mid off.
Length delivery outside off, Watling tries cutting it but it's too close to play that shot. Chops it towards the point fielder.
Fuller and attacking the stumps, pushed towards the fielder at mid on.
Fuller in length and swinging back in on middle and leg, Watling walks across and works it through square leg for a couple of runs.
Fuller delivery in that channel outside off, the batter lifts his bat to let it be.
Hits the deck hard, but it's too high for anyone. Latham just lets it sail over his head.
Angles one in from outside off, Tom covers the line and shoulders arms again.
Back of a length in the channel outside off, Tom is happy to let it pass.
Wood goes short, angles it in on middle and leg, Tom ducks.
Short of a good length, outside off, Latham shoulders his arms.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the Kiwi keeper.
Sprayed wider on off, nothing doing, says BJ.
Stokes keeps it full again outside off, driven towards cover.
Gets forward to a fuller delivery and eases it to mid off.
Another one on a fuller length outside off, blocked.
Fuller ball from over the wicket, angling in, BJ defends it towards cover by prodding ahead.
Ben Stokes is introduced into the attack.
Angling in on middle and off, bunted back to Mark Wood off the front foot.
Stays back to a length delivery outside off, Tom Latham shows the full face of the bat.
TL chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Edge which doesn't carry! On a length and outside off, a bit of away movement on that one. Tom pokes at it with soft hands and gets an edge which goes on the bounce to Root at second slip.
Another one outside off, Tom doesn't pay any heed to it.
From around the wicket comes Wood, hurls it outside off, Tom shoulders his arms.
Flighted ball on off, pushed towards cover again. 9 off the over.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Watling drives this fuller ball towards cover.
FOUR! Dropped short outside off, Watling stays back and cuts it past point for the second boundary of the over.
Nudges it towards backward square leg and picks up a single.
FOUR! Swept again! A bit fuller on middle and leg, Tom is quick to get down on one knee and sweeps it neatly past the man at short fine leg for a boundary to start the over.
Fuller and tailing back in a tad late, clipped towards the square leg fielder off the inner half.
Fullish in length by going wide of the crease, BJ works it to mid on.
Hits the deck hard, BJ Watling is happy to sit under it and let it sail over him.
Shout for an LBW! Fullish delivery, swinging back in on middle, Watling gets an inside edge on the pads. It's starting to reverse now.
On a back of a length outside off, stabbed out in front of the cover fielder.
Wood comes into the attack and bangs in a short one first up. It's heading down leg as the batsman easily ducks under it.
Takes a stride ahead and defends it down well.
Latham plants his front foot across and leaves it alone.
Loopy delivery outside off, defended into the ground.
Stays back and blocks it out.
Flatter through the air, Tom goes back to defend but the ball takes the inside edge and goes on the bounce to short leg. Lucky!
FOUR! Shot of the day for me! He's such a good play of spin, Latham. Floated delivery outside off, Tom gets down and sweeps it disdainfully in front of square for a boundary.
Once again Anderson hurls one on the pads, BJ flicks it towards mid on for nothing.
Harmless length ball outside off, defended down.
Fuller on the pads, glanced down to fine leg for a single.
Stays back footed and stabs it out.
Touch fuller in length on middle and leg, defended towards the leg side.

One James errs in line, the other James errs in the field. The latter is having a really tough time in the field since yesterday. Fuller delivery, a bit too straight from Anderson. Watling clips it towards Vince at square leg who fumbles and concedes a run. The bowler isn't happy with that effort.
Comes from around the wicket and tosses it up on the stumps, it's pushed with an open face of the bat towards short third man.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Fullish on off, defended in front of FSL.

Missing the stumps by a long away! Waste of a review from England. Leach pitches it on the rough outside off and a puff of dust was seen coming off. The ball then turns in sharply and pings Tom on the pads who is across the stumps to defend it. Huge appeal but nothing from the umpire. Leach convinces his skipper to go for the review and England take it. Hawk Eye shows it's hitting in line but would have gone miles down leg.
A long and hard appeal for an LBW against Tom Latham has been turned down. Jack Leach is very interested and he convinces his skipper to take the review.
Leans ahead and smothers it away.
Fuller ball on off, Latham defends it well.
FOUR! Fuller and on the pads, Watling gets across and flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Good timing on that.
Fuller delivery on off, BJ defends it well.
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, Watling offers a stoic defense.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
On a length again, Watling pushes it away.
Length ball outside off, defended off the back foot towards cover.
Flighted delivery, fuller in length on off, the batter presses forward and smothers it away.
TL defends it from within the crease.
Beaten! Lands it on the rough, Latham goes back to play for the turn but this goes straight on with the arm. Beats the outside edge by justtttttt....
Low full toss, darted in on the stumps, wristed away towards wide mid on for a single.
Takes a stride forward and defends it well.
Slower through the air, landing around off, Tom prods forward to defend but gets an inside edge. Luckily for him it flies past the left of short leg for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, Watling comes across before making a leave.
Gets forward to a full delivery and pushes it to mid on, off the inner half again.
Full and tailing back in on middle and leg, Watling looks to flick but gets it off the inner half behind square on the leg side for a couple.
Outside off, pretty harmless, left alone by BJ.
Another one hurled on the same length, Watling is tight in defense.
Good length delivery on middle and off, a compact defense from Watling.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Floated delivery outside off, Latham comes forward to defend but the ball trickles away off the inner half past short leg for one.

FOUR! Nailed it! A half century for Tom Latham, his 14th in Tests and he seems to be the only silver lining in this Kiwi innings, at least for now. Gets down to a tossed up delivery and cracks a sweep shot in front of square on the leg side. A raise of the bat from him but he knows the job is really a big one ahead.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Goes back and clips it with the turn towards the leg side.
Outside off, defended into the ground.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Watling stays back in defense. A successful over from Jimmy comes to an end.

Drinks break. What a fabulous morning for England! They claimed four wickets in the first hour and have completely demolished the Kiwi top order. Stuart Broad initiated it by picking back-to-back wickets first up and then the debutant, Jack Leach removed Ross Taylor to gain his maiden wicket. The last wicket of Henry Nicholls further dented New Zealand's hope of saving this Test as England continue to dominate. Tom Latham has fought bravely but is losing partners quite quickly. Will he get some support? BJ Watling has joined him who played a superb knock in the first innings. Let's see how the next hour pans out.

OUT! Anderson induces an edge! Just when I said he's not looking at his usual best today, he comes in and shuts my mouth completely to put England in complete command. Henry Nicholls departs this time. Jimmy entices the batter by keeping it nice and full outside off, asking him to go after it. Henry does so with hard hands and the ball shapes away a bit to take the thick edge. Alastair Cook, who at first slip is waiting in anticipation, takes the catch safely. We usually talk about the batsman not taking his front foot forward enough while attempting to drive. You cannot fault Henry much here for his footwork but his head wasn't getting forward enough with his stride which brought his downfall. All going England's way.
Fullish delivery on off, defended down watchfully.
Fuller and sprayed wider outside off, Nicholls has got nothing to do with it.
Another one on a similar length, this time it's Nicholls who works it around the corner for a couple more. James isn't at his usual best today.
On a back of a length on middle and leg, Latham clips it through square leg for a single.
James Anderson is back into the attack.
Pitches it on the rough outside off, right in the business is Leach, says Atherton on air. Nicholls takes a long stride forward as he buries it into the ground.
Just past Stokes at slip! Quicker delivery, angling in and then straightening a bit, Henry goes back to defend but gets it off the edge past Stokes at first slip for a brace.
More loop from Leach, landing full on off, defended into the ground.
Is right forward to a tossed up ball as Henry blocks it out.
Lunges ahead to a loopy delivery and gets an inside edge towards short leg.
Drifting in from around off, Nicholls stays back and defends it on the bounce to short leg.
More like it but it's too short to trouble the batsman. Nicholls gets back and helps it to mid-wicket for a single.
Identical to the last one, once again Henry allows it through. Root needs to get closer to off stump.
A touch shorter and outside off, skidding in, Henry takes his front leg forward and leaves.
Strides forward to a full ball and blocks it back.
Bowling with two slips now. He serves it full and on off, Henry squeezes it out through backward point for a couple.
Floated and full on off, Nicholls with a big lunge defends it to the off side.
FOUR! Flatter this time and shorter as well. Latham reads it well, goes on the back foot and slaps it through cover-point for a boundary.
Loopy and on off, Tom gets forward in defense.
Flighted and too full on middle, it's defended back to the bowler again.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Strong shot but it was in the air for a while. A flighted full ball on off, Latham kneels and sweeps it aerially over square leg for a boundary.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Shot! Root drops it short outside off, Henry cuts it nicely through point for a boundary.
Henry Nicholls avoids a pair! Is a bit cramped for room as this one is darted in on off, he still manages to punch it towards cover. The fielder there misfields and concedes two.
Henry presses forward in defense.
Flattish in nature, Henry shows a straight bat.
From around the wicket, fuller on the stumps, kept out.

Joe Root brings himself on! Spin from both ends then. There is something in the pitch for the spinners and the English skipper decides to have a go. Maybe, there are two left-handers out there so this could be another reason. Also, there is a case of bowling Dawid Malan. He bowls leggies and can get sharp turn into the lefties from the rough outside off.
A bit short and turning in, Tom goes back to defend but the ball beats the outside edge of his bat.
Flatter delivery, turning in from around off, Tom hangs back and keeps it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Slower through the air, landing full on off, Tom blocks it out.
Loopier and fuller again on off, Tom presses ahead in defense.
Very full on the footmarks outside off, Latham presses ahead in defense.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Latham taps this length delivery in front of cover and calls Nicholls through for a quick single. The fielder has a shy at the striker's end but misses.
Latham shoulders arms to let that one through.
Good length delivery, close to off stump line. Tom hangs his bat out in defense but it goes off the edge which rolls through the slip cordon. A couple taken.
Fuller in length on off, Latham is solid in defense.
Bangs in a short one on middle, Latham ducks.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Henry Nicholls is the new man in. He is on a pair.

OUT! Jack Leach removes Ross Taylor. Maiden Test wicket for him and it's a huge one. Impressive captaincy from Joe Root, you got to give it to him. Taylor played a sweep shot on the first ball of the over which prompted Root to keep Alastair Cook at short backward square leg, not a usual field placement, somewhere between short fine leg and a proper backward square leg. It has worked wonders! Flighted delivery, not that full to be swept but Taylor wants to. He does so but off the top edge and it's a simple catch for the former English captain. Celebrations go wild. New Zealand in tatters now. Also, Leach has broken the deadlock for England, first bowler in this Test apart from the new ball bowlers to pick a wicket. Yesterday, Colin de Grandhomme did the same.
Flighted delivery outside off, swept powerfully through square leg for a single.
Quicker fuller ball outside off, defended down solidly.
Goes back and tucks it with the spin towards the leg side.
Flighted delivery outside off, Taylor gets across and paddles it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Brings one back in on middle and leg, worked away towards mid on. Tidy stuff from Stuart, giving nothing away.
Sprayed wider outside off, Latham watchfully makes another leave.
Lets the ball pass outside his off stump without much fuss.
Another one on a fuller length, Latham drives it crisply but couldn't get it past mid off.
Fuller in length on off, punched towards mid off.
Angling away from the southpaw, Latham knows where his off stump is as he makes a good leave.
Loopy delivery outside off, a nice push into the cover region.
Drifting in from around off and then straightening a bit, Latham stays back footed this time to pat it away. Gets it off the edge which rolls away towards point and they take one.
Tom Latham takes a stride forward and kills it down.
Quicker through the air at 87 kph, Latham has got nothing to do with it as it was outside the off stump.
Floated delivery outside off, Tom presses ahead and drives it neatly through covers for a couple of runs.
FOUR! A gentle loosener to begin with for Leach! Flatter and shorter outside off, Latham is quick to rock back and latch onto it. He punches it firmly through covers and picks up a boundary.
Early change as Root brings his spinner on. It's Jack Leach to have a go now.

FOUR! Slapped! That should ease the nerves for Ross. Ahead of a length and with width offered outside off, Taylor leans ahead and smacks it through cover-point for a blazing boundary. Can he make the dropped catch count? Well, his side would be hoping for it to happen big time.
Fullish on off, driven towards mid off.

Edged and Vince drops another! Yes, another. He dropped one yesterday offered by Tom Latham and hands a life to Ross Taylor now. This could be a big moment in the game. Broad can't believe it, he almost had another. Walks towards his run-up area with his head down. Fuller in length, just around off and moving away a bit. Taylor without any feet movement goes hard at it. Gets a fat edge which travels quickly towards third slip where Vince dives to his left but fails to hold on. It hits his palms and trickles behind which allows them to take a couple more.
Waits for the fuller ball to come back in and then knocks it towards mid on.
In the channel outside off, Ross Taylor lifts his bat to make a leave.
On middle and leg, nudged through the vacant mid-wicket region for a single.
Full and straight on the stumps, driven on the up towards mid on.
Served a bit wide outside off, easy leave for the senior man.
Hangs back and shows a straight bat in defense.
Edgeddddd! Fuller in length and angling in from around off, Taylor looks to defend but it takes the outside edge and rolls towards the slip cordon.
Good length delivery, coming back in on middle, worked towards the on side.
A bit short in length on middle and leg, tucked through mid-wicket for a single. 50 up for the Kiwis.

Broad goes wide of the crease and angles in a fuller delivery on the stumps, Taylor looks to work it away but does so off the inside edge down to fine leg. Easy two taken as there is no one manning that area.
Beaten! Fuller again and curling in a bit, Taylor lunges forward to defend but it straightens and beats the outside edge of his bat by a whisker.
FOUR! Shot! This is a really good shot from Ross! Fuller again from Broad, angling in, Taylor brings his bat down in time and knocks it past mid on for a boundary to open his account.
Pounds in a short one after bowling two full deliveries, Taylor is quick to duck under it.
Fuller again, just outside off, Ross Taylor lunges ahead and defends it off the straight bat.
Good delivery again! Stuart Broad has his tail up. Fuller ball, angling in from outside off, it keeps coming in, Taylor plants his front foot across and leaves it alone.
Anderson gets to over the wicket and delivers a full ball in the line of the stumps. Latham is watchfully behind the line in defense.
Back of a length delivery around off, Latham covers the line and shoulders arms.
A bouncer this time, around middle and leg, easily picked by Latham as he lets it go to the keeper.
And again. Tom is not going to chase those. He leaves it untouched and unattended outside the off stump. Anderson should look to get close to the off stump line.
Left alone outside off. Anderson is trying to suck him into some kind of drive. So far, Tom has restrained.
Angles in a shortish ball on off, Tom is behind the line as he defends it solidly. New Zealand need him to stay. His style of batting is what they need, stoic and stubborn.
Starts by overstepping. Bowls it on a good length outside off, Latham makes a watchful leave.
James Anderson to operate from the other end. The best possible start for England and they will hope that Jimmy joins the party as well. Four slips in place...
In the avenue of bamboozlement, Taylor shoulders his arms to it. Double-wicket maiden for Broad, England off to a flying start.
Short of a length delivery on middle, a bit of extra bounce as Taylor hops back and defends it down on the pitch.
Good length delivery in the channel outside off, Ross is happy to make a leave.
Taylor negotiates the hat-trick delivery. Fuller in length and angling in on middle, Ross closes the face of the bat and works it towards the square leg fielder.
Ross Taylor, the second big shot as David Lloyd would call him is out next to face the hat-trick ball. Five slips, a short leg and a short cover in place.

OUT! Edged and Kane Williamson is out of here. My word, Stuart Broad, you freaking beauty. He's on a hat-trick now. New Zealand have been rocked early on Day 5. If the previous delivery wasn't a great one, this was almost unplayable. Short of a length ball, angling in at first and then seaming away off the deck with a bit of extra bounce. Williamson hangs back to defend it but the away movement catches the tiny part of the outer blade and settles into the gloves of Bairstow behind. Huge appeal and the finger has been raised. Golden duck for Kane and this could be a bit of pain for his side. Also, you don't want to give early wickets to Broad, he is a rhythm bowler and if he tastes blood early, he just tears through the batting line up. Barmy Army is very vocal, they are singing the Broad anthem - He's big, he's bad, he's better than his dad - Stuart Broad, Stuarrtt Broaddd... hahaha!
Kane Williamson is the new man in. The skipper comes in early and has a job in his hand.

OUT! Gone first ball! Stuart Broad has struck. All the hard work done by Raval yesterday evening has gone down the drain. What a start for England! This wasn't a wicket-taking delivery by any means but the visitors wouldn't mind it at all.
